history.title: History length
history.description: How long Sediment keeps history. It deletes data older than this. It thins newer data in place and never removes it early.

data.custom_days: Custom length (days, used when you pick Custom)

resolution.title: Sediment resolution
resolution.description: How finely Sediment keeps old history. **Fine**: 15 minutes up to 1 year, 1 hour up to 3 years, then 6 hours. **Standard**: 15 minutes up to 6 months, 1 hour up to 2 years, then 6 hours. **Coarse**: 1 hour, 6 hours, then 1 day. Every resolution keeps spikes, steps, every state change and gaps where a sensor was unavailable.

data_description.size_cap_gb: A guard only. If the projected size is above the cap, Sediment offers a coarser oldest tier. It never thins newer data to fit.

tiers.title: Custom tiers
tiers.description: Three tiers, newest first. A tier lasts until the age you give. The last tier lasts to the end of the history length. The bucket is the time window in which Sediment keeps the extremes.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.description:
Every entity has one profile. **keep**: never thinned. **default**: thinned with the resolution you chose. **coarse**: wider buckets and a shorter horizon. **drop**: kept for the raw window only, then deleted.

One rule per line, first match wins: `selector = profile [flap|noflap]`. A selector is an entity id with `*` and `?`, or `domain:sensor`, `device_class:temperature`, `integration:my_integration`. `flap` or `noflap` overrides the flapping collapse for those entities. Lines starting with `#` are comments.

Example: `sensor.cpu_* = coarse`

{rule_errors}

data_description.flapping_collapse: When on, Sediment reduces a burst of four or more state changes, each within a minute of the last, to its first and last change. This applies in the tiers from 1 hour on. When off, Sediment keeps every change.

purging.title: Purging and retention
purging.description:
The recorder currently keeps **{keep_days} days**, its automatic purge is **{auto_purge}** and its automatic repack is **{auto_repack}** (as configured when Home Assistant started).

Tick the box to let Sediment take over purging. Sediment then turns off the recorder's own nightly purge. It deletes events, short-term statistics and recorder runs itself, but not earlier than the recorder would have. It thins states instead of deleting them, and removes them only after the history length.

Once the takeover is applied, **thinned history depends on it**. If the recorder's purge came back, it would delete everything older than {keep_days} days at its next nightly run. Switching **dry run** on later only pauses thinning. The takeover stays applied. If the integration cannot work (for example after a Home Assistant update it was not tested with), it keeps the recorder from purging and raises a repair issue. Unticking the box asks for confirmation. Removing the integration hands purging back and tells you. Disabling it keeps purging off until Home Assistant restarts.

Safety net: add `recorder: auto_purge: false` to `configuration.yaml`. Sediment cannot protect your history if it fails to load at all. The built-in purge then runs.

While **dry run** is on and the takeover is not applied yet, Sediment computes everything, writes a report and deletes nothing. The recorder keeps purging as before.

data_description.takeover: Needs a recorder version Sediment was tested with and a SQLite database. Otherwise nothing changes, and a repair issue explains why.
data_description.raw_days: The newest rows stay untouched for this many days.
data_description.dry_run: Compute and report only. Untick to start thinning for real.

confirm.title: Projected size
confirm.description:
With these settings the database would be about **{projected_gb} GB** after {years} years ({rows_m} million state rows). Size cap: {cap_gb} GB.

The estimate starts from your recorder's real row rates and the built-in reference measurements. After a dry run it uses this installation's own numbers.

confirm_over_cap.title: Projected size
confirm_over_cap.description: The projection of **{projected_gb} GB** is above your cap of **{cap_gb} GB**. Tick the box to make the oldest tier coarser and recalculate. Sediment never thins newer data to fit. Submit without ticking to keep the settings as they are.

confirm_over_cap_final.title: Projected size
confirm_over_cap_final.description: The projection of **{projected_gb} GB** is above your cap of **{cap_gb} GB**. The oldest tier is already as coarse as it goes. Shorten the history, raise the cap, or continue anyway.

release_confirm.title: Hand purging back?
release_confirm.description: Sediment owns purging at the moment. If you untick the takeover, Home Assistant's own purge turns on again. At its next nightly run (about 04:12) it **deletes everything older than {keep_days} days**. That includes all thinned history older than that. Tick the box only if you want that.

data.release: Yes, release purging and accept that older history is deleted

error.invalid_tiers: Tier 1 must end before tier 2, and buckets must not shrink with age.

takeover_blocked.title: Sediment cannot take over purging
takeover_blocked.description:
Sediment is set to take over the recorder's purging. But this Home Assistant version or database differs from what Sediment was tested with. So Sediment left the recorder as it is: {reasons}

Sediment changes nothing while this issue is open. Update Sediment, or untick the takeover in its options.

takeover_protecting.title: Sediment keeps the recorder from purging
takeover_protecting.description:
Sediment has taken over purging, but it cannot work with this Home Assistant version or database: {reasons}

To protect the thinned history, the recorder's automatic purge stays off, and Sediment thins and deletes nothing. Update Sediment. If you remove Sediment, purging goes back to the recorder. The recorder then deletes everything older than its configured keep days.

unsupported_database.title: Sediment supports SQLite only
unsupported_database.description: {reason}. Sediment does not take over purging and does not thin or delete anything on this database. A dry run, which only reads, still works. If Sediment had taken over purging before, the recorder's automatic purge stays off.

safety_net.title: Safety net: stop the built-in purge in configuration.yaml
safety_net.description: Set `recorder: auto_purge: false` in `configuration.yaml`. Then a failed Sediment load cannot hand your history to the built-in purge. Sediment takes over purging only after it has started. If it does not load (a failed update, a missing file), the recorder runs its own nightly purge and deletes everything older than its keep days.

job_failing.title: Sediment's nightly job keeps failing
job_failing.description:
The nightly job has failed {count} times in a row. Last errors: {errors}

Nothing is lost. Sediment retries the failing step, and the history length and cleanup steps still run. Check the log and the report in `sediment/last_report.json`.

retention_inferred.title: Sediment found old history and holds the purge back
retention_inferred.description:
Sediment found states that are {days} days old, older than the {keep_days} days the recorder keeps. Sediment cannot tell whether it thinned them earlier. So it holds back Home Assistant's own purge to protect them. This is safe: nothing is deleted.

If Sediment never thinned this database (for example you lowered the recorder's keep days), untick the takeover in the options. Sediment asks you to confirm, because the built-in purge then deletes everything older than {keep_days} days at its next nightly run.

run_now.name: Run now
run_now.description: Run the thinning job once, outside the nightly schedule.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Compute and report without deleting. Leave empty to use the integration's setting.

clear_quarantine.name: Clear quarantine
clear_quarantine.description: Thin again, on the next run, the entity-days that Sediment skipped after errors.

export_profile_map.name: Export profile map
export_profile_map.description: Write <config>/sediment/profile_map.json: entity, resolved profile, the profile signature and its hash. tools/merge_history.py --profile-map uses it so the import knows the profiles that only Home Assistant can see (integration, registry).

import_history.name: Import history
import_history.description: Import older history from a file made by tools/merge_history.py. Sediment inserts only rows older than the oldest live row. A dry run reports and writes nothing.

path.name: File
path.description: Path of the import database. Put it in <config>/sediment/.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Report what would be imported and write nothing. On by default.
